transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-01
Start time: 15:00 UTC (scheduled 45m)
Duration: ~47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Miles Carter (CSM), Avery Nguyen (Solutions) — Tom Abernathy (Valence Procurement), Leila Moreno (Valence Security), Samir Gupta (Valence Platform), Hannah Cho (Valence Legal), Ravi Iyer (Valence DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, rough):
- Purpose: sprint-style handover for vendor onboarding and to align MSA/DPA redlines, SLA thresholds, KMS/egress expectations, and trial/pilot technical scope.
- Key risks: data residency/egress fee clarity, KMS key custody, SLA latency buckets for inference at 95th percentile, procurement wants fixed pricing tier for pilot.
- Agreed immediate next steps: Redwood to send redline, SE to run quickbench and share cost/latency tradeoffs, customer to provide data classification and security contacts.

Topics covered:
- DPA/MSA redline expectations and exceptions
- Private deploy vs dedicated capacity for regulated workloads
- KMS/HSM options and privileged keying
- Egress billing and fee tiers for high-throughput inference
- Pilot scope, benchmarks, and connectivity (VPC peering / private link)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Okay everybody, um, thanks for hopping on. I'll kick off, we have a compact agenda — legal redlines, S L A matrix, and then a fast technical handoff for the pilot. Tom, you wanted to start with procurement priorities?
[00:17] Tom (Procurement): Yeah thanks, Jordan. Quick note — procurement is focused on three things: fixed pilot pricing, MSA exceptions we can't accept at enterprise level, and clear termination / data return language. We're not trying to slow things down but we need the redlines early.
[00:36] Jordan (AE): Totally, got it. We'll put those front and center. Priya, can you outline the pilot connectivity options?
[00:44] Priya (SE): Sure — for the pilot we recommend either Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private depending on the residency needs. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and no additional networking work, but if you need customer-managed VPC we'll do Private (V P C peering or Private Link). For KMS, we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (bring your own K M S / H S M). I should say, some customers call that privileged keying, some call it BYOK.
[01:10] Leila (Security): Quick Q — with BYOK, do we get audit logs for key usage exported to our SIEM? And is the key ever in Redwood control?
[01:21] Priya (SE): Good Q — with customer-managed keys, Redwood never holds plaintext, keys stay in the customer's KMS— we provide op-level audit hooks and can stream key usage logs (subject to the log retention policy). There's some nuance — if you want H S M-backed keys in your cloud, we can integrate. We'll include an audit log sample in the security pack.
[01:44] Samir (Platform): Follow-up on that — network path latency matters a lot. If we go with Private via V P C peering, what are the usual 95th pct latencies for 8k token prompts?
[02:01] Priya (SE): In our experience with similar accounts, 95th falls in the 120–250 ms range for non-quantized medium models on dedicated GPU pools. That widens if you add shorter batching windows or cross-region routing. We'll provide an empiric matrix — though final numbers depend on your token lengths and batch strategy.
[02:22] Jordan (AE): Note — customer's asking for an SLA at 99.9 for availability and a latency SLO for 95th pct. Internally we have different tiers; I'll map those to Redwood SLA tiers.
[02:33] Hannah (Legal): On the DPA side — Valence needs to carve out certain healthcare data categories. We have a couple of mandatory clauses for data retention and audit frequency. Are those usually exceptions?
[02:44] Miles (CSM): We see that frequently; normally we can accept retention limits and stricter deletion windows in Private deployments when needed. There may be commercial implications for long-term retention or cold storage.
[02:55] Tom (Procurement): Also the customer is pressing on egress fees — especially since we'll hit heavy inference traffic during the pilot. We need a predictable egress band or a cap.
[03:05] Priya (SE): Understood. For pilots we often propose a fixed egress allowance and after that a tiered fee. We'll put a documented egress schedule in the pricing appendix.
[03:16] Leila (Security): Another point — SSO and provisioning. We need SAML/SCIM for RBAC. Can you confirm provisioning latency? We want automated user sync.
[03:28] Avery (Solutions): Yes, we support SAML S S O and SCIM for provisioning. Onboarding for an initial admin group usually completes within 48 hours once SAML config is provided.
[03:36] Jordan (AE): Great. Let's move to the MSA / DPA redlines — Tom and Hannah, what are the non-starters?
[03:44] Hannah (Legal): We can't accept open-ended indemnity changes and we'd prefer a 60-day termination for convenience. Also we need clarity on subprocessors list, and the DPA must explicitly name data categories.
[03:56] Jordan (AE): We can take a look. Redwood's standard MSA has carveouts, but we'll call them out. We'll push a redline and flag anything that is commercial vs legal.
[04:06] Tom (Procurement): One more — escrow / continuity. If Redwood gets acquired, we need a continuity plan and code or model escrow?
[04:15] Jordan (AE): We can discuss continuity and an SLA-backed exit path; code/model escrow is uncommon but we can see if commercial team can surface options.
[04:23] Leila (Security): About SOC 2 and ISO — do you have recent reports? We'll need an attestation and SOC 2 Type II report for our audit team.
[04:33] Miles (CSM): Yes, we can share SOC2 Type II and ISO certs through an NDA/portal. We'll note that in next steps.
[04:42] Samir (Platform): Technical deep dive — for the pilot can we get a containerized quickbench or do you need us to send sample prompts?
[04:50] Priya (SE): We prefer sample prompts to set realistic sequence lengths, plus a small runner script. We'll share a quickbench repo link. For inference, we leverage KV cache and continuous batching; note devs sometimes see "K V cash" in transcripts — sorry, that's a little ASR artifact — but KV cache is important for prefix caching savings.
[05:08] Ravi (DevOps): For connectivity, we prefer AWS Private Link. Is that supported?
[05:14] Priya (SE): Yes, Private Link and VPC peering are supported; Private Link often reduces cross-account network complexity and can lower egress noise. We'll include a connectivity checklist.
[05:25] Hannah (Legal): On DPA redlines — can Redwood accept alternate security auditors or do you only accept a set list?
[05:33] Jordan (AE): We accept reputable auditors; we'll share our standard portal and the auditor list, but we're flexible with valid evidence.
[05:40] Tom (Procurement): Pricing note — we need a capped pilot spend at $20k unless we mutual agree to expand. Is that something Redwood can accommodate?
[05:48] Jordan (AE): We can propose a pilot package that stays within a fixed spend — we'll outline a package that maps to tokens / embeddings / throughput and a hard cap.
[05:58] Leila (Security): Any red flags around PCI or PHI? We are mostly dealing with protected health info in some flows.
[06:06] Priya (SE): For PHI we recommend Redwood Private with customer-managed keys; also we recommend on-prem or VPC deployment depending on your egress/residency rules. We'll highlight PHI patterns in the security pack.
[06:20] Samir (Platform): Ops question — does Redwood provide audit logs for model inference calls at token level? We need request-level tracing for compliance.
[06:30] Priya (SE): We provide request metadata and tracing hooks. Token-level traces are heavier — usually we provide per-request meta and a checksum. If you need full token traces that's an escalated support add-on — we'll explain tradeoffs.
[06:42] Jordan (AE): I'll mark that as an action item to include a trace sample in the security docs.
[06:48] 
[09:10] --- mid call jump (note: transcription timestamps are approximate; some ASR dropouts around 07:20-09:00) ---
[09:20] Priya (SE): Back to SLA specifics — typical Redwood SLA for Dedicated is 99.9 availability with credits for dropouts; latency SLOs are usually published per model profile. For enterprise we'll attach a tailored SLA with penalty caps.
[09:41] Hannah (Legal): Penalty caps — procurement wants to know max liability and whether that aligns with our buyers table.
[09:50] Miles (CSM): We'll propose standard liability limits and we can discuss enlarging for enterprise contracts under commercial negotiation.
[10:04] Samir (Platform): For the pilot scale — what is the fastest route to scale to production if we like the pilot? Dedicated pool expansion or multi-region routing?
[10:15] Priya (SE): Usually both. We start with dedicated capacity, then add burst pools and multi-region replicas for geo failover. We also recommend prefix caching and batch tuning to hit cost targets.
[10:26] Tom (Procurement): Ok if we accept initial redlines and pilot cap, timeline is: procurement sign-off by 11/12, pilot kickoff week of 11/15, evaluate after 4 weeks. Is that realistic?
[10:36] Jordan (AE): Yes, that's realistic contingent on legal signoff and connectivity tests. We'll aim to have documents out by 11/04 so your legal team has time.
[10:44] Leila (Security): We'll want a short security questionnaire response and architecture diagram before pilot.
[10:50] Avery (Solutions): We'll attach an architecture diagram and a security questionnaire; expect those in the same zip as the redline.
[11:00] 
[20:12] Tom (Procurement): A note on subprocessors — we need a list for the DPA. If Redwood uses third-party inference infra partners or cloud providers, list them and the data location.
[20:25] Jordan (AE): We'll provide a subprocessors list and clarify if data leaves region. On Redwood Private the customer controls region.
[20:33] Hannah (Legal): For the MSA section 7, we propose a 180-day notice for data export requests. Is that something Redwood typically does?
[20:41] Miles (CSM): 180 days is longer than typical; we can propose a reasonable window and include an escalation path for urgent data export requests.
[20:49] Leila (Security): Also, can you enumerate retention deletion windows? We need to map that to our internal retention policy.
[20:56] Priya (SE): We'll include a retention table — live request logs vs audit logs vs model artifacts and typical deletion timeframes.
[21:05] Jordan (AE): Quick clarification on billing — do we need any commitment to get a dedicated pool for the pilot?
[21:12] Priya (SE): For short pilots no long-term commit needed; we can reserve modest dedicated capacity for trial but for guaranteed sustained throughput you do commit to a reserved capacity plan. We'll detail options.
[21:25] Ravi (DevOps): If we go dedicated, how are upgrades to runtime handled? Is there forced downtime?
[21:33] Priya (SE): We do rolling upgrades with canary and automatic fallback; downtime is rare and we publish maintenance windows. We'll include the upgrade runbook.
[21:44] 
[33:02] Hannah (Legal): One last legal nuance — indemnity for data breaches, we want narrower carveouts. Procurement and security aligned on this.
[33:10] Jordan (AE): We'll flag indemnity as a negotiation point and separate commercial vs legal terms in the redline.
[33:18] Tom (Procurement): Okay final ask — could Redwood include an explicit egress cap during pilot to avoid surprise invoices?
[33:25] Jordan (AE): Yes, we'll include a pilot egress cap and a notification flow if it's near the cap.
[33:34] Leila (Security): And send sample SOC2 and auditor contact info under NDA.
[33:39] Miles (CSM): Will do.
[33:45] Priya (SE): I'll also prepare the quickbench repo, and a short doc on KV cache best practices and batch sizing—that should help show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[33:58] Samir (Platform): If we see a bad regression in model quality after quantization, what's the rollback path?
[34:06] Priya (SE): We maintain version pinning and automatic fallback to the unquantized model variant; we'll also run quality evals tied to your prompt-sets.
[34:16] Jordan (AE): Great. Let's capture next steps and owners — we'll go to the action items.
[34:24] Miles (CSM): I'll send meeting notes and include links: redline docs, SOC2 portal link, quickbench repo, connectivity checklist.
[34:35] Tom (Procurement): Thanks all.
[34:36] Jordan (AE): Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the package and set the pilot kickoff once redlines land.

Meeting close at ~15:47 UTC.
